results:
The fan spray tip recovered equal to higher DNA than the M-Vac for most samples (5/7) which was significant for the gloss painted wall.

The shower tip recovered comparable DNA yields on 4/7 substrates.

Authors suggest the PLS system is a viable alternative to the wet-vacuum due to comparable DNA yields and cost-effectiveness on substrates where swabbing may have failed to recover sufficient DNA for profiling.

substrate_descriptions: Glass slide (Fisher Brand)
results: Diamond™ Dye (DD) was used to visualise the cellular material recovered with the adhesive lifter and masking tape. No STR profiling was performed. results:

The wet-vacuum had an average of 12 times the DNA yield as the swab.

substrate_descriptions: PVC pipe section, 9 V battery, electrical tape, and copper wire.
results:
Swab types are most influencial factor for allele recovery.

Swab comparison: Different swabs combined with specific wetting agents work better for different substrates. For example the  Puritan DNA-Free Forensic Cotton Tipped Applicator with deionized water for electrical tape and the EO cotton swab with lysis buffer for PVC pipe sections. 

Substrate study: For batteries the Puritan DNA-Free Forensic Cotton Tipped Applicator moistened with PBS, SDS, and deionized water had consistently higher DNA yields than other swabs.

Puritan nylon flocked & Hi-VAN Lab cotton swab did not recover DNA from all substrates, regardless of the wetting agent.

TL  versus swab comparison: EO cotton swab had the highest median DNA recovery percentage (20.8%), Solar tape (11.2%) but was not statistically significant. They were both significantly more efficient than thre sellotape and officeworks tape (p < 0.05).

Pre-post protocol study: The post-study implemented protoccol significantly improved the STR profile quality (p < 0.01).

results:
Carpet: DNA yield highest for TL. This was signiicant compared to the DNA-Buster (p <0.01) and M-Vac® (p< 0.001). Full profiles were obtained for TL, Swab & dry vacuum.

Sweater:  DNA yield highest for M-Vac®, but was the most variable. Significant to SWS (p < 0.001), TL (p < 001). Full DNA profiles for TL, & both vacuums, but more complex mixtures with the vacuums.

Stone: DNA yield highest for swabbing compared to tape (p < 0.01) and to both vacuums (p < 0.0001). There were significantly higher % full profiles for swab.

Tile: Similar results to the stone substrate.

Wood: TL had the highest DNA yield (significant to swab & DNA-buster) & significantly higher % full profiles.
